text:
anya: Heads-up — hit a repeat failure while seeding a fresh onprem node. Operator evicted the seed pod mid-transfer when disk pressure spiked. Result: partial seed, operator marked node degraded, manual intervention required.

josh: ugh. do we have a reproducible step? or was that a real customer repro?

anya: customer repro. steps: start seed, interrupt with `dd` to fill disk on node, operator observes pressure, issues eviction to keep control-plane healthy. seed resumes but files missing.

maria: eviction on pressure seems right for control-plane safety, but we should differentiate "seed-critical" vs normal pods. seeds need a higher grace window + restart semantics.

kevin: agree. proposal: operator treats seed transfer as a resumable idempotent stream. eviction should trigger a stateful checkpoint and backoff, not a hard delete.

anya: exactly. minimal contract: 1) seed sends chunked manifest with checksums 2) operator persists last-acked offset before eviction 3) on restart, seed resumes from offset rather than restart whole transfer.

josh: +1. what's the UX for operators? we need observable state transitions: RECEIVING -> PAUSED -> RESUMING -> APPLIED. also show last-acked offset in console.

maria: also need eviction policy flags. e.g.:
```yaml
seedPolicy:
  evictionGraceSec: 300  # default extended grace
  maxRetries: 6
  backoff: { base: 5s, factor: 2 }
  allowEvictIf: [criticalPod, emergency]
```
kevin: that looks reasonable. but we still need to handle partial blobs: if a blob upload is interrupted, we should upload to a temp chunk store and commit on final checksum verification. partials are garbage collected after `evictionGraceSec` + retry window.

anya: garbage collection is key. current GC runs on normal retention which deleted partially uploaded shards and left the node in a weird state. We should add a per-seed tombstone lifecycle: 1) tombstone with TTL 2) operator keeps tombstone until retries exhausted 3) if user explicitly aborts, tombstone allowed to be GC'd immediately.

josh: ops-bot suggestion: emit an event when seed enters `PAUSED` with reason `DiskPressure` and include `resume_after` ETA. That way SREs know not to force-delete.

ops-bot: deploy:seed-state-events v0.3 deployed to staging (172.31.9.12). See /deploy logs. :white_check_mark:

maria: about retries — we need bounded total time for a seed transfer. open-ended retries tie up operator slots. config should include `maxTotalRetryWindow: 24h` and `maxAttempts: 6`.

kevin: we also need a backpressure signal upstream: if many seeds are paused, throttle starting new seeds and surface a cluster-level warning. Otherwise we overload the cluster trying to catch up.

anya: good call. propose circuit-breaker: if pausedSeeds > N or pausedRatio > 20% then pause new seeding and surface guidance in Console with recommended ops steps.

josh: ops playbook snippets: 1) check paused seeds `kubectl get seed -o wide` 2) inspect last ack `kubectl describe seed/<name>` 3) if node disk full, run `sudo du -sh /var/lib/seeder` and free space OR cordon node and move seed to healthier node. 4) if stuck, use `operator seed-resume --force <id>` after verifying partial checksums.

maria: we should provide a helper `seed-checksum-verify` binary in the airgap bundle so customers can verify partial blobs locally before forcing resume. small, static Go tool.

kevin: question: do we need on-disk durability guarantees on the receiver side? i.e., write-ahead log for chunk receipts. If the node reboots during transfer we can replay. increases complexity but makes resume safer.

anya: lightweight WAL makes sense. keep it in same data dir and make it compact after commit. WAL format: {seedID, offset, chunkHash, committed}. simple.

josh: one more UX detail: Console should show estimated resume size and ETA based on historical bandwidth. helps SRE decide to wait vs redeploy seed.

maria: agree. also expose a `forceAbort` action with audit log so enterprise customers can record the manual cancel.

kevin: ok next steps: 1) RFC a minimal operator contract for seed checkpoints + eviction grace 2) add config knobs (`evictionGraceSec`, `maxRetries`, `maxTotalRetryWindow`) 3) implement WAL + temp chunk store + commit flow 4) console events + pause-circuit breaker 5) include small `seed-checksum-verify` binary in airgap bundles.

anya: I'll draft the RFC today and ping this thread with a link. tagging @josh @maria for review.

josh: thanks — please include a short migration plan for existing partials (GC TTL bump + one-time reconcile job).

maria: will review. also add test scenarios for flaky disks (noise tests).

kevin: thanks all. great catch, anya.
